hero.title: Electric Go-Kart Engineering Portfolio
hero.descriptor: An integrated vehicle engineering portfolio presenting spaceframe chassis design, Ackermann steering kinematics, hydraulic braking, and electric powertrain integration with comprehensive analytical derivations and ANSYS FEA simulation contours.
hero.imageAlt: Complete isometric CAD assembly of the electric go-kart.

subsystems.title: Chassis & Spaceframe Structure
subsystems.subtitle: Tubular spaceframe architecture, roll hoop, and crashworthiness
subsystems.design: Fabricated from AISI 4130 Chromoly steel tubes (OD 25.4 mm, 1.65 mm wall thickness; Yield: 460 MPa, UTS: 560 MPa). The chassis links the occupant cell, side impact protection rails, seat anchor points, and rear powertrain cradle into a continuous triangulated loadpath for maximum torsional rigidity and impact energy absorption.
subsystems.approach: ANSYS 2026 R1 was used to conduct static structural impact analyses (frontal 44.8 kN, lateral 33.6 kN) and torsional stiffness simulations. Direct application of dynamic crash loads in static solvers introduces artificial stress concentrations (26.5 GPa); therefore, nominal member stresses are verified analytically against material yield limits.

subsystems.title: Steering System & Kinematics
subsystems.subtitle: Ackermann geometry, stub arm, knuckle, and tie-rod linkage
subsystems.design: Designed with a central steering column, pitman arm, adjustable stainless-steel tie rods, and SS304 steering knuckles. The geometry coordinates the front wheels to follow concentric arcs during cornering, eliminating scrub and reducing tire wear.
subsystems.approach: Kinematic equations relate the inner steering angle (32.19°) to the outer steering angle (21.32°) using the wheelbase (1060 mm) and front track width (1032 mm). Static structural FEA was performed on the knuckle (mild steel, Yield: 250 MPa), stub arm (SS304, Yield: 215 MPa), and tripod joint under maximum kingpin moments of 11.53 N·m.

subsystems.title: Hydraulic Braking System
subsystems.subtitle: Master cylinder, caliper hydraulics, and disc thermal dissipation
subsystems.design: Features an adjustable pedal box (5:1 mechanical leverage), a 17 mm bore master cylinder, steel-braided hydraulic lines, and a single-piston floating caliper acting on a ventilated 200 mm diameter stainless-steel rotor mounted to the live rear axle.
subsystems.approach: Hydraulic line pressure, caliper clamping force, disc frictional braking torque, and deceleration were evaluated from an initial velocity of 60 km/h (16.67 m/s). An ANSYS transient thermal analysis (10 s braking cycle, h = 50 W/m²·K) confirmed maximum disc temperatures of 205.7°C, well below the thermal limits of SS304.

subsystems.title: Electric Drivetrain & Live Axle
subsystems.subtitle: PMSM motor, chain reduction, EN24 live axle, and battery system
subsystems.designTitle: 5.0 kW PMSM Traction & Live Axle Drive
subsystems.design: Driven by a 72V 5.0 kW PMSM motor (Peak Torque: 78 N·m, 3200 RPM) paired with a FOC controller. Power is transferred via an alloy-steel roller chain reduction (15T drive to 42T driven sprocket, ratio 2.80) to a slotted, stepped EN24 alloy-steel rear live axle.
subsystems.approach: Longitudinal vehicle dynamics were evaluated including aerodynamic drag (Cd = 0.70, A = 0.85 m²), rolling resistance, and acceleration forces (0–50 km/h in 4.0 s). The live axle was modeled in ANSYS under combined motor torque (207.5 N·m) and reverse braking torque (335 N·m) to verify fatigue limits.
